newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-FINLAND BEAT SLOVAKIA TO JOIN MEDALS HUNT.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-FINLAND BEAT SLOVAKIA TO JOIN MEDALS HUNT.

text.p: Finland beat Slovakia 5-2 in the world ice hockey championship on Friday to join Russia, the Czech Republic, Sweden and the United States in the final series next week.
The sixth team in the medals hunt will be Canada or Italy, who meet on Saturday in a match to decide third place in pool B in Turku.

The six finalists will start the medals hunt on the points earned in preliminary round games against other teams in the final series. From pool A, the Czechs are certain to start on two points from their win against Finland.
Russia have two points from their win over the Czechs, and may start on four if they beat Finland on Saturday. A draw would see Russia start on three points and Finland on one.
"Two points for us when we go into the final series would be very important in order to reach the final in this tournament," Finnish coach Curt Lindstrom said after the win over Slovakia.
"It is very important to try to win tomorrow," he said.
Of the pool B finalists, Sweden were held to a surprise 1-1 draw by underdogs Latvia on Friday but have defeated both Canada and Italy.
The United States have lost to Canada but beaten Italy. On Friday, Norway held Italy to a 2-2 draw. The U.S. play Sweden on Saturday in a game deciding the starting points for both.
Friday's loss sent Slovakia to join Germany and France from pool A in the relegation play-offs in Tampere. Latvia and Norway, and Canada or Italy, will go to Tampere from pool B.
Finland took the lead in the 15th minute as Juha Lind stormed between two Slovak defenders to pick up a cross-ice pass and circle goalkeeper Pavol Rybar to shoot into an empty net.
Midway through the second period, Slovakia's Jergus Baca failed to stop a pass and the puck bounced from his left skate into his own net. The goal was given to Finn Mika Nieminen.

Baca atoned for his mistake, setting up the first Slovak goal with a thundering power-play slapshot in the 38th minute. Finnish goaltender Jarmo Myllys failed to hold the shot and Lubomir Kolnik snapped up the rebound.

Kai Nurminen put Finland 3-1 up but Slovakia quickly struck back. Jiri Bicek's low shot from a close angle whizzed past Myllys. Two minutes later Finland were 4-2 ahead, the goal scored by Nieminen, who pushed the puck across the line at the near post.
Numminen's hard slapshot completed Finland's scoring in the 55th minute.
In earlier pool A action, Roger Dube scored twice and took the lead in the scoring statistics with five individual goals as France beat Germany 2-1.
